problem_text:
A telecommunications network must establish a low-latency fiber optic ring connecting six major data hubs.

The signal propagation delays between hubs are measured in milliseconds:
* Hub Alpha to Hub Beta: 51.0 ms
* Hub Alpha to Hub Gamma: 48.8 ms
* Hub Alpha to Hub Delta: 157.4 ms
* Hub Alpha to Hub Epsilon: 202.4 ms
* Hub Alpha to Hub Zeta: 168.3 ms
* Hub Beta to Hub Gamma: 83.8 ms
* Hub Beta to Hub Delta: 106.6 ms
* Hub Beta to Hub Epsilon: 151.4 ms
* Hub Beta to Hub Zeta: 117.6 ms
* Hub Gamma to Hub Delta: 180.3 ms
* Hub Gamma to Hub Epsilon: 224.3 ms
* Hub Gamma to Hub Zeta: 189.6 ms
* Hub Delta to Hub Epsilon: 44.9 ms
* Hub Delta to Hub Zeta: 12.0 ms
* Hub Epsilon to Hub Zeta: 34.7 ms

The objective is to identify the minimal total propagation delay circuit that interconnects each hub precisely once before completing the cyclic path back to the initial hub.
